title: Podaraki, Grecia, tutorial di Juancarlos Battilani

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: Juancarlos Battilani teaches in a structured and calm manner, directly addressing the camera while demonstrating steps from an elevated angle. He breaks down the dance into clear lateral and central variations, combining verbal explanation with physical demonstration.

lesson_structure.note: Introduction by the teacher in a red shirt and red beret
Introduction of the dance Podaraki from Greece
Demonstration and counting of the lateral part
Explanation and demonstration of the central part (part B)
Full practice of Podaraki to music

extraction.counting_scheme: un e due e tre pam pam

steps_taught.name: parte laterale
steps_taught.description: lateral stepping movement starting with free right foot

steps_taught.name: parte centrale
steps_taught.counts: un cia un cia un cia cha
steps_taught.description: central variation practicing right and left free foot leads

quotes.text: La danza che vorrei presentarvi oggi si chiama Podaraki.
andiamo verso destra faremo un e due e tre pam pam.
La parte B della danza è invece può essere sul posto.

evidence_segments.observation: The teacher speaks directly to the camera wearing a red shirt and red beret.
evidence_segments.cannot_infer: exact spatial layout of the room off-camera

evidence_segments.observation: The teacher steps laterally while counting aloud with arms in W position.

extraction.distinctive_method: Using an overhead camera view consistently throughout the instructional breakdown to clearly show foot placement and patterning on grid-like tiles.
